journal_prompts: What is on my mind right now?
What happened today that I want to remember?
What am I worried about, and what is in my control?
Something I am grateful for is...
If a friend felt like this, what would I tell her?

guides.title: Exam stress: small steps that help

sections.p: Pick one subject and study for 25 minutes, then rest for 5. A small start is easier than a big plan.
Sleep, water and real meals help your memory more than one more late night.
Breathe slowly for one minute before you start and before the exam. Try the Breathe tool in the Care tab.
Tell a lecturer, friend or counsellor if it feels too heavy. Asking early is a strength.

guides.title: When you do all the group work

sections.p: Write who does which part, with dates, in the group chat on day one.
Send a short reminder: 'Hi, can you share your part by Thursday?'
Save the messages. If someone does not take part, you can show your lecturer calmly.

guides.title: Speaking up when someone takes credit

sections.p: After meetings, send a short email: what you did and what is next. It leaves a clear record.
Try: 'I worked on this part, happy to explain it.' Say it in the moment or in a private chat.
Share your progress in writing now and then, so your work is seen.

guides.title: Asking for a raise without feeling awkward

sections.p: List what you achieved this year and what you took on beyond your role.
Look at what similar jobs pay. Job sites and colleagues in other companies can help.
Choose a calm time. Say what you achieved, and what you would like. Then listen.

guides.title: Staying safe when you travel alone

sections.p: Tell someone your route and when you expect to arrive. Charge your phone.
Share your live location with a friend. Check the plate and driver name of a ride before you get in. Sit behind the driver if you can.
Wait inside a shop or a lit place, not on a dark street.
Go to a busy place, call someone, and call 999 if you are in danger.

guides.title: If someone online pressures you for photos

sections.p: You can say no. Do not send anything you are not comfortable with.
Save screenshots, block the person and report the account on the app.
Talk to a trusted person or a helpline in the Care tab. It is not your fault.

guides.title: When you feel low for a while

sections.p: Many women feel low, tired or numb at times, especially when they carry a lot.
Sunlight, a short walk, a regular meal, a message to a friend. Small steps count.
If the feeling lasts for weeks, stops you doing daily things, or you have thoughts of hurting yourself, please talk to a doctor or call a helpline now. You can find numbers in the Care tab.

guides.title: Talking to your family about hard things

sections.p: Choose a calm time, not during a fight or a busy day.
Try: 'I love you, and I want to share something that matters to me.'
They may need time. You can say, 'Let us talk again tomorrow.'
If it is not safe to talk, speak to a trusted adult, a counsellor or a helpline.
